lessons.title: Certification checklist and your 90-day data plan
objectives: Confirm your capstone evidence is complete before the final quiz
Build a weekly data habit that takes about 30 minutes
Write a 90-day plan with measurable targets
Choose the next spreadsheet skills to learn

blocks.text: You are close to finishing. This lesson helps you check that your capstone is complete, prepare for the final quiz, and turn what you have learned into a routine that keeps paying off after the certificate.
How certification works

To receive the **Certificate of Completion in Data Literacy**, you must complete the practical capstone and score at least **70%** in the final quiz. The final quiz has 12 questions, so you need at least 9 correct answers. The app asks you to confirm that your practical task is complete before you submit the quiz.

blocks.title: Capstone evidence checklist
items: Five-sheet workbook
Cleaning log and dictionary
Summary and two charts
One-page report
90-day plan
blocks.caption: Tick each item before you open the final quiz.

blocks.text: Prepare for the final quiz

items: Re-do one calculation of each kind: mean and median, percentage, percentage change, gross margin and break-even.
Remember which chart fits which question: bars compare, lines show change over time, pies show a few parts of a whole.
Review the cleaning tools: TRIM, PROPER, COUNTIF for duplicates, COUNTBLANK, dropdowns.
Review honesty and privacy: response rates, sampling bias, correlation and causation, anonymising data.

blocks.name: certification
blocks.caption: Your certificate confirms both your practical workbook and your understanding of the methods.

blocks.text: A weekly data habit

Skills fade if they are not used. The simplest way to keep them is a short weekly routine at a fixed time, for example Sunday evening or Monday morning. Thirty minutes is enough for a small business or group.

items: Enter or check the week's records and fix any errors (10 minutes).
Look at your dashboard: are your 3 to 5 KPIs on target? (5 minutes)
Look for one surprise: the highest or lowest number, or a change from last week (5 minutes).
Write one decision for the coming week (5 minutes).
Once a month, do a longer review with a chart and share a short summary with your partner, team or group.

blocks.title: Worked example: a 90-day plan
blocks.context: For example, Halima (from Module 1) finishes the course and wants to grow her kiosk. Today her average weekly revenue is about ₦95,000, her gross margin is about 24% and she has no record of repeat customers.
steps: Days 1 to 30: record every sale in Google Sheets with a dropdown for item and payment method; set up a dashboard with weekly revenue, gross margin and stock-outs.
Days 31 to 60: start a simple customer list (with permission) to measure repeat customers; review supplier prices and aim to raise gross margin from 24% to 26%.
Days 61 to 90: use the data to test one change, such as a small bulk-buy discount for two weeks, and compare with the two weeks before.
Targets for day 90: 12 weeks of complete records, gross margin at least 26%, a repeat customer rate measured for the first time, and one tested change with a written result.
blocks.result: Her plan is specific, measurable and based on her own data. At day 90 she can show, with numbers, what changed and what she learned.

blocks.text: Making targets measurable

A target is useful only if, at the end of the period, you can say clearly whether you met it. "Grow my business" cannot be checked. "Raise gross margin from 24% to 26% by the end of December" can. Each target should name the metric, the starting point, the goal and the date. Keep the number of targets small, three is plenty, so that you actually track them every week.

head: Vague goal
Measurable target
rows: Record 100% of sales in Google Sheets for 12 weeks in a row
Raise gross margin from 24% to 26% by day 90
Measure repeat customer rate monthly and reach 50% by day 90
Cut late deliveries from about 12% to under 5% next quarter

blocks.text: Some weeks will go badly: a power cut wipes out a day of trade, or you forget to record sales during a busy festive week. That is normal. Note what happened in your log, fill in what you can from bank alerts and receipts, and continue. A record with a few honest gaps is far more useful than no record at all.
What to learn next

items: **Lookups:** VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP to pull a price or name from another table automatically.
**Pivot tables:** fast summaries by category, month or branch.
**Google Forms linked to Sheets:** clean data collection from customers or members.
**Looker Studio:** Google's free tool for building shareable dashboards from your sheets.
**Free tutorials:** the GCFGlobal Google Sheets tutorial covers these skills step by step.

blocks.title: Share what you know
blocks.text: Teaching one other woman in your group to keep a tidy sales log is one of the best ways to strengthen your own skills, and it raises the quality of data your group relies on.

takeaways: Certification needs the capstone plus at least 9 of 12 in the final quiz.
A 30-minute weekly routine keeps your records and skills alive.
A good 90-day plan has dated steps and measurable targets.
Next skills: lookups, pivot tables, Forms and Looker Studio.

activity.title: Finish and plan
steps: Go through the capstone evidence checklist and complete anything missing.
Choose a fixed weekly time for your data routine and put a reminder on your phone.
Write your 90-day plan with three phases and at least three measurable targets.
Choose one next skill and find a free tutorial for it.
activity.evidence: Your completed checklist and written 90-day plan with targets.

quiz.q: Which sheet in the capstone workbook should never be edited?
quiz.explain: The Raw sheet keeps the original records so you can always check or redo your cleaning. All changes happen in the Clean sheet.

quiz.q: Ngozi's revenue was ₦260,000 in August and ₦315,000 in September. Which is the best finding statement?
options: Revenue grew about 21% from August to September
September was the best month ever
quiz.explain: (315,000 minus 260,000) ÷ 260,000 × 100 = about 21.2%. A finding states what the data shows with a number and a period.

quiz.q: A programme trained 45 women; 25 of the 38 graduates now keep weekly records. Which of these is an outcome?
options: 25 graduates now keep weekly sales records
quiz.explain: Outcomes are changes that happened because of the work. Enrolment, sessions and completion are outputs.

quiz.q: What should come first in a one-page report to a busy manager?
options: The main message in one sentence
quiz.explain: Lead with the answer. Method and details go at the end or in an attachment.

quiz.q: The final quiz has 12 questions and the pass mark is 70%. What is the minimum number of correct answers?
quiz.explain: 70% of 12 is 8.4, so you need at least 9 correct answers.

quiz.q: Halima wants to test whether a bulk-buy discount increases sales. What is the fairest approach?
options: Start the discount and also change suppliers and opening hours at the same time
Run the discount for two weeks, keep other things the same and compare with similar weeks before
Ask one friend if she thinks it worked
Look only at the best day during the discount
quiz.explain: Changing one thing at a time and comparing with similar periods gives a fairer test of cause and effect.

finalQuiz.q: Which of these is categorical data?
finalQuiz.explain: Payment method is a label from a short list. The others are numbers you can add or average.

finalQuiz.q: Daily sales are ₦10,000, ₦12,000, ₦11,000, ₦13,000 and ₦60,000 (a wedding order). Which figure best shows a typical day?
finalQuiz.explain: Sorted, the middle value is ₦12,000. The one wedding order pulls the mean up to ₦21,200, which does not describe a typical day.

finalQuiz.q: Which practice best protects a shared contribution register?
options: Share it with "Anyone with the link can edit"
Post screenshots in the group chat each month
Use member codes, share as Viewer and turn on 2-Step Verification
Keep it only in a paper notebook with no copy
finalQuiz.explain: Codes reduce exposure of personal data, Viewer access prevents accidental changes, and 2-Step Verification protects the account.

finalQuiz.q: In a tidy data table, how should "3 bags rice" be recorded?
options: Exactly as written in one cell
Quantity 3 in one column and Item Rice in another
As a comment on the cell
finalQuiz.explain: Tidy data puts one fact in each cell and one variable in each column, so the spreadsheet can calculate with the quantity and group by item.

finalQuiz.q: Which formula adds the amounts in column E only for rows where column B says Beans?
finalQuiz.explain: SUMIF checks the first range for the condition and adds matching values from the third range. COUNTIF only counts.

finalQuiz.q: A trader wants to show what share of her sales comes from each of four products. Which chart fits best?
options: Pie chart or sorted bar chart
finalQuiz.explain: With only four parts of one whole, a pie chart works; a sorted bar chart also compares the shares clearly.

finalQuiz.q: A list has the same receipt number on three rows. Which tool flags these quickly before deleting?
finalQuiz.explain: The COUNTIF helper shows TRUE for any value that appears more than once, so you can review duplicates before removing them.

finalQuiz.q: A survey link shared only on WhatsApp gets few replies from older members with basic phones. What is this problem called?
finalQuiz.explain: Sampling bias happens when the people who respond differ from those who do not, so the results lean one way.

finalQuiz.q: Revenue is ₦250,000, cost of goods sold ₦190,000 and running costs ₦15,000. What is the net profit?
finalQuiz.explain: Gross profit is 250,000 minus 190,000 = ₦60,000. Net profit is 60,000 minus 15,000 = ₦45,000.

finalQuiz.q: A flyer says an investment platform paid "30% every month" and shows a steadily rising chart. What should she do first?
options: Invest a small amount to test it
Treat it as a warning sign and check registration with the SEC Nigeria
Trust it because there is a chart
finalQuiz.explain: Fixed, high monthly returns backed by charts and screenshots are classic signs of a Ponzi scheme. A chart is not proof.

finalQuiz.q: Which statement is an outcome rather than an output?
options: 60% of graduates were keeping weekly sales records three months later
finalQuiz.explain: Outcomes are changes that followed the work. Sessions, enrolment and flyers are things delivered (outputs).

options: Raise gross margin from 24% to 26% by the end of December
finalQuiz.explain: A measurable target names the metric, starting point, goal and date, so you can check whether it was met.

capstone.title: Data cleaning and insight workbook
capstone.brief: Build a five-sheet Google Sheets workbook from at least four weeks of real records (your business, group or workplace, with permission), clean it, summarise it, chart it and write findings, then present them in a one-page report and a short WhatsApp summary, with a 90-day plan.
steps: Write one clear question and list the data you need to answer it.
Collect at least four weeks of real records into a Raw sheet and copy them to a Clean sheet.
Clean the data with TRIM, PROPER, COUNTIF and COUNTBLANK, add dropdowns, and keep a cleaning log and data dictionary.
Build a Summary sheet with totals, counts, shares, mean and median, and at least three business or programme metrics.
Create two charts with message titles, units and honest axes, and test them on one person.
Write up to three findings and one recommendation, including limits of the data.
Prepare a one-page report and a WhatsApp-length summary, gather feedback from one person, and write a 90-day plan with measurable targets.
evidence: Screenshot of the five sheet tabs and the question

Summary sheet with category totals that match the overall total
Two charts, before and after feedback
Short reflection on what changed after feedback
90-day plan with at least three measurable targets
